sources.report:
About this data

These videos are previews rendered by OriginFlow: the egocentric camera with per-finger force traces (left and right hand), a hand-pose overlay, head and wrist trajectories, and an annotation timeline (episode, subtask, atomic action). The raw streams are not part of this folder, so the viewer shows the renders as delivered, downsampled from 120 to 30 fps.

Data quality, as reported by the provider

Frame-level validity flags over the OriginData preview dataset (10,867,077 frames). They count valid or detected frames; they do not measure force or pose accuracy.

FieldMeaningRate
left.force_validLeft-hand force values valid99.84%
right.force_validRight-hand force values valid99.84%
observation.hand.left.detectedLeft hand detected93.24%
observation.hand.right.detectedRight hand detected96.09%
observation.head.pose_validHead pose finite and aligned (not tracking quality)100.00%

Real-robot training results, as reported by the provider

Eight tasks trained from scratch (starVLA with a DiT-B head, batch 32; 641 sequences over 10 tasks, 525 train / 116 test): after 20,000 post-training steps the mean success rate was 34.35% with force input and 28.30% without. Squeezing salad dressing with 50,000 pretraining and 10,000 post-training steps: 75% (15/20) with force, 55% (11/20) without. Gains vary by task; stamping went from 15% without force to 10% with it.

sources.title: EgoTactile
sources.about: A right-hand pressure glove with a head- or neck-mounted egocentric camera, single grasps of 63 everyday objects by 12 participants, plus a bare-hand subset.

hardware.d: 4×3 fingertip pads, one strip per finger, 72-taxel palm · 0–350 N · about 17 Hz, held on a 15 Hz clock
Released at 1280×720 · 15 fps
Plus participant sex and hand length

sources.notes: Paper: arXiv 2606.09243 · project egotactile.github.io · code github.com/Russell-Zeng/EgoTactile. Videos are re-encoded to H.264 and redistributed under CC BY-NC 4.0 with attribution; the release ships MPEG-4 Part 2, which browsers cannot play. The glove model is not named in the paper. In the bare-hand subset the pressure comes from a synchronized off-camera gloved grasp.

sources.title: OpenTouch
sources.about: Egocentric in-the-wild recordings with a full-hand tactile glove on the right hand, Aria glasses video and Rokoko hand pose: 5.1 hours, 2,900 annotated clips in 14 environments.

hardware.d: 16×16 electrode grid, 169 taxels on fingers, thumb and palm (palmar side) · 30 Hz
RGB; 640×480 JPEG frames in the release · 30 fps · re-encoded here
21 hand landmarks + wrist and palm position · 30 Hz
Per clip, with contact onset, peak and post-contact frames

sources.notes: Paper: arXiv 2512.16842. The code repository's package metadata says MIT; the release states no license for the data, which is shared from Google Drive. The sample videos are re-hosted here for preview with attribution. Raw readings are 3072 at rest and fall with pressure; the viewer shows 3072 − raw, uncalibrated.

sources.title: HATO
sources.about: Teleoperated bimanual UR5e arms with two Psyonic Ability hands, six touch sites per fingertip; four tasks: banana handover, block stacking, wine pouring, steak serving.

sources.notes: Paper: arXiv 2404.16823; code github.com/toruowo/hato; data on Berkeley Box (linked from the code README). The release states no license; the sample videos are re-hosted here for preview with attribution. Videos are built from the RGB frames stored in each step's pickle; depth is not shown. In the converted episodes the right hand's middle fingertip reads zero throughout, and some steps carry corrupted touch bytes (handled as described in each episode's notes). The wine-pouring task is not shown: every pour episode sampled had the right hand's touch bytes corrupted in most steps.

sources.title: ADL-21
sources.about: Tactile signatures of the right hand in 21 activities of daily living: a 361-sensel Tekscan Grip pressure sensor on a glove, 22 subjects performing each task once (462 trials). Touch only, no video.

hardware.d: Thin resistive pressure sensor, 361 sensels in 18 regions on the volar right hand · 4 mm pitch · 0–517 kPa map · 50 Hz

hardware.v: Sensor sewn on a cotton glove
hardware.d: Covered by a polyethylene and a latex glove during the tasks
GF, CGF and pressure on a 101-step time-warped timeline, per trial
No video, hand pose or object pose

sources.notes: Paper: Sensors 21(8):2594, 2021, doi:10.3390/s21082594 (CC BY). Data: one MATLAB file on Zenodo, CC BY 4.0. Pressure maps are drawn on the release's own sensor map (a palmar view of the right hand), shown as force per sensel (kPa × 16 mm²). The release's grip force (GF), per-region share (CGF) and synchronized pressure exist only on the authors' time-warped 101-step timeline; they are mapped back to each trial's 50 Hz clock here by inverting the documented warp (derived, approximate).

sources.notes: Paper: arXiv 2303.12076 (CoRL 2023). No license or terms of use were found for the data (project page, GitHub README and repository, Drive folder); the arXiv licence covers only the paper. The release is two zips on a public Google Drive folder; each sampled recording is read from them by byte range. Camera videos are the release's AVIs re-timed by their frame timestamps, re-encoded to H.264 and re-hosted. All tactile pads are shown in the release's own pad layout (one column per finger), with per-pad (x, y, z) sums as arrows; which Allegro finger each of columns 1-3 is, and which slot is the fingertip, is not documented. The Allegro PD efforts and Kinova joint efforts are plotted.

hardware.d: Coaxial piezoresistive fibres inlaid orthogonally in a machine-knitted glove · 32×32 grounding-based readout (Arduino Nano) · ~14 Hz · raw 10-bit counts, uncalibrated

No video, hand pose or task description

sources.notes: Paper: Nature Electronics 4, 193–201 (2021), doi:10.1038/s41928-021-00558-0. Data: two zip archives in the project page's open Dropbox folder; no license or terms are given for the data (the code repository has no LICENSE), so the collection is labelled "License not stated". Readings are raw ADC counts shown above each cell's rest level; readings above 1,000 are replaced as in the authors' code. The glove layout is the release's own drawing, documented for the calibration glove and inferred to fit the object recordings; the vest and KUKA sleeve layouts are the release's own files too (the sleeve's 3-D positions are unrolled onto a plane by the converter).

sources.title: ActionSense
sources.about: Kitchen activities recorded with wearable sensors: bimanual 32×32 conductive-thread tactile gloves, finger and body tracking, forearm EMG, eye tracking with a first-person camera, plus 5 static cameras; 20 activities, 10 subjects (tactile for S00–S05).

hardware.d: Palm 23×19, thumb 5×9, little 11×4, other fingers 13×4 · raw ADC counts · ~6 Hz · open fingertips
1280×720 ~30 fps head-mounted · 1600×1200 22 fps static (one above the table)

hardware.v: Xsens MTw Awinda + Manus Prime II gloves
hardware.d: 17 IMUs, body and finger segments at 60 Hz · Myo EMG 8 ch per forearm
Plus calibration periods (scale presses, held objects) and experimenter notes

sources.notes: Paper: NeurIPS 2022 Datasets & Benchmarks (openreview olvz0gAdGOX). Data CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial, credit, same license); code MIT. Each episode is one labelled activity instance cut out of the release's continuous per-split files and re-encoded here. The matrix-to-hand placement of the taxels is derived from the data (non-crossing matrix entries barely respond), not from a published map; see each episode's notes. Up to six right-glove crossings toggle between rest and ~1018 (an intermittent read-out fault, not contact); they are flagged per episode from the data, drawn hollow and left out of the plots and sums.
